quirks: Darlaston births are registered under the Walsall civil registration district (not West Bromwich). Always search the Walsall district GRO index for Darlaston events.
West Bromwich births are registered under the West Bromwich civil registration district. A family moving between the two towns will have children registered in different districts.
Darlaston All Saints chapelry was created in 1872 from the ancient Darlaston St Lawrence parish. Post-1872 baptisms may appear in either register; search both.
GRO indexes are filed by the quarter of registration, not the date of birth. A birth on 20 March registered on 6 April appears in the April-June quarter.
It was common English practice to reuse a child's Christian name if the first child with that name died in infancy. Search burial registers alongside baptism registers for the same given name.

The GRO website (gro.gov.uk) provides the mother's maiden name on birth index searches for free — most third-party sites do not show this for pre-1911 records. Use the GRO site to confirm a match belongs to the right family.

The 1911 census (just outside the target period) asks the wife for total children born alive, still living, and deceased — a direct count that can surface all births including those that left no other surviving record.
Darlaston had four Wesleyan places of worship. Search Nonconformist registers (held at The National Archives and on Ancestry/FamilySearch) if a child is not found in Anglican registers.

Records from this period are in Staffordshire Record Office (pre-1974). Post-1974 the area became West Midlands; Sandwell Archives holds some later local authority records but not the historical registers.
Neighbouring parishes include Wednesbury and Walsall. A child baptised near a parish boundary may appear in a neighbouring register; search these if not found in Darlaston or West Bromwich registers.
The Darlaston Weekly Times (1882-1887) at Findmypast may carry infant death or birth notices for children who do not survive to census years.
Staffordshire Name Indexes (staffsnameindexes.org.uk) is a locally-maintained volunteer index worth consulting alongside national databases.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: West Bromwich and Darlaston, Staffordshire, England (1875–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview

- West Bromwich is an ancient parish and civil registration district in the South Offlow hundred of Staffordshire. The civil registration district of West Bromwich was created in 1837. In 1974 the area transferred to West Midlands.
- Darlaston is an ancient parish (records from 1539) in the South Offlow hundred. Its civil registration district is Walsall — not West Bromwich.
- County archive: Staffordshire Record Office. Ecclesiastical diocese: Lichfield, Province of Canterbury.
- Economy: Iron and steel manufacturing, bolt and nut making, coal mining (Black Country).
- Religious denominations: Church of England; strong Wesleyan Methodist presence (four Wesleyan places of worship in Darlaston); Baptist; Roman Catholic (Birmingham Archdiocese).

## Boundary changes

- Both towns in Staffordshire throughout 1875–1900; transferred to West Midlands in 1974.
- Critical registration split: West Bromwich births filed under West Bromwich district; Darlaston births filed under Walsall district. Search both.
- Darlaston All Saints chapelry established 1872 from ancient St Lawrence parish; post-1872 baptisms may appear in either register.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- National civil registration began 1 July 1837 (England_Civil_Registration wiki). Mandatory with penalties from 1875 onward; coverage 1875–1900 is essentially complete.
- Registration districts: West Bromwich → West Bromwich district; Darlaston → Walsall district.
- Free access: FreeBMD (freebmd.org.uk), GRO website (gro.gov.uk), FamilySearch collection 2285338.
- Subscription: Ancestry collection 8912 (births 1837–1915); Findmypast; Staffordshire BMD indexes (Ancestry collection 61709).
- GRO certificates must be ordered from GRO; index alone is freely searchable.

### Church records

- Darlaston St Lawrence: registers from 1539; Bishop's Transcripts from 1660.
- Darlaston All Saints (chapelry): established 1872.
- West Bromwich All Saints: registers from 1608; chapelries St Paul (1853) and St Peter (1858).
- West Bromwich Christ Church: registers from 1829.
- West Bromwich Holy Trinity: registers from 1841.
- FamilySearch digitized Darlaston church records (32 volumes total, first page returned): key volumes covering 1875–1900 are 100885191 (All Saints baptisms 1891–1905, 100% indexed), 102021571 (1854–1900, 100% indexed), 102021572 (1885–1898, 100% indexed), 102021568 (1883–1891, 100% indexed), 102021569 (1891–1899, 100% indexed).
- Pre-1886 Darlaston baptism microfilm volumes (007566563/007566564 series): 0 images online; physical microfilm only.
- Staffordshire-wide: FamilySearch collection 2364451 (1538–1944, indexed + images); Ancestry collection 62292 (baptisms 1813–1900); Findmypast Staffordshire Baptisms.

### Census records

- 1881 (April 3), 1891 (April 5), 1901 (March 31) — all indexed + images online, free at FamilySearch.
- No state or off-year census for England.
- 1911 census (FamilySearch collection 1921547) asks wife for total children born, living, and deceased — critical for family completeness.

### Cemetery records

- James Bridge Cemetery, Darlaston (opened 1860): burial registers 1860–1908 digitized at FamilySearch (full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed — must browse image by image).
- Cemetery records 1860–1991 and 1888–1970: multiple FamilySearch volumes, full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed.
- Burial register index 1860–1976 available (volume 008072650_010, 68 images).
- Monumental Inscriptions of St Lawrence, Darlaston and Wesleyan Methodist Church, Pinfold Street at FamilySearch Catalog.
- West Bromwich: Monumental Inscriptions of Christ Church Graveyard at FamilySearch Catalog.

### Newspaper records

- Darlaston Weekly Times, 1882–1887 at Findmypast — birth, death, and marriage notices.
- British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk) for wider West Midlands coverage.

### Other records

- Poor rate books, Darlaston, 1893 (FamilySearch volume 008068830_003, 432 images, full-text searchable).
- School records: Staffordshire Record Office; not comprehensively online.
- Probate: England & Wales National Probate Calendar 1858–1995 at Ancestry (collection 1904).
- City/county directories at Ancestry (collection 1547) for year-by-year address location.

## Repository guide

### Online
FamilySearch (free), FreeBMD (free), GRO online (free index), Ancestry (subscription), Findmypast (subscription), Staffordshire BMD / West Midlands BMD (free), FreeReg (free).

### Physical
Staffordshire Record Office, Eastgate Street, Stafford ST16 2LZ — original parish registers, Bishop's Transcripts, Poor Law records, school records.
General Register Office, Southport — original civil registration certificates.
Sandwell Archives — post-1974 local authority records.

## Research tips

- Darlaston births are under Walsall registration district. Search both Walsall and West Bromwich in FreeBMD and GRO.
- Use the GRO website directly for free access to mother's maiden name on birth index entries (not shown on most third-party sites pre-1911).
- Search 1881, 1891, and 1901 censuses for all household members; the 1911 census provides a fertility summary.
- Search burial registers alongside baptism registers — infant name reuse was common.
- Darlaston had four Wesleyan places of worship; search Nonconformist registers if not found in Anglican records.
- Darlaston Weekly Times (1882–1887) may carry infant death notices.
- Check neighbouring parishes Wednesbury and Walsall if not found in Darlaston/West Bromwich registers.
- Staffordshire Name Indexes (staffsnameindexes.org.uk) is a locally-maintained volunteer index worth checking.

entry.rationale: Completeness question: did Hannah Earnest and Edwin Grice have children beyond John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James? The couple lived in West Bromwich and Darlaston, Staffordshire. Key constraint from loc_001: Darlaston births register under Walsall civil registration district, not West Bromwich — all birth-index searches must cover both districts. The 1911 census fertility count is the strongest single corroborating source. Infant deaths before census year must also be checked (the death index) as a child who died in infancy would leave no census trace. Nonconformist chapel registers are separately required given Darlaston's strong Wesleyan presence.

entry.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: The 1881 census (FamilySearch collection 2562194, name-searchable, personCount 30,000,000+) lists every person in each household on 3 April 1881. Search for Edwin Grice as head of household in West Bromwich and Darlaston. All children resident on census night appear by name and age. The known children span c.1877–1886, so this census captures those born by early 1881 and still living. Any additional child born before April 1881 and alive on that date would appear here. Priority 1 because it is free, indexed, and directly enumerates the household.

entry.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: The 1891 census (FamilySearch collection 1865747, name-searchable) lists the household on 5 April 1891. By this date all five known children would be between approximately 5 and 14 years old if still living. Any additional child born between 1881 and 1891 and surviving to that date would appear here. Comparing the 1881 and 1891 household rosters reveals children who appeared in one census but not the other — evidence of a birth and death between enumeration years. Search Edwin Grice as head in West Bromwich and Darlaston.

entry.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: The 1901 census (FamilySearch collection 1888129, name-searchable) lists the household on 31 March 1901. Older children may have left home by this date; youngest children born in the 1890s would still be resident. Cross-referencing all three census households (1881, 1891, 1901) provides a near-complete picture of children who survived to at least one enumeration year. Children appearing in 1901 but absent from both earlier censuses would indicate a birth in the 1891–1901 window.

entry.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: The 1911 census (FamilySearch collection 1921547, name-searchable) is the single strongest source for family completeness: it explicitly asked the wife to state the total number of children born alive, those still living, and those who had died. Hannah Earnest's answer provides a direct count that can reveal children not otherwise traceable (infants who died young, children who emigrated, or children who died between census years). Any discrepancy between her stated count and the number of children identified across all other sources flags remaining gaps.

Any discrepancy between her stated count and the number of children identified across all other sources flags remaining gaps.

entry.rationale: England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008 (FamilySearch collection 2285338, name-searchable). Search for all children with surname Grice registered in the West Bromwich civil registration district from 1875 to 1900. The mother's maiden name (Earnest) appears on the GRO index and confirms family membership. This is the primary documentary source for every birth, including children who died before any census year. Registration was essentially complete and legally enforced from 1875. Note: Darlaston births are under the Walsall district — see pli_006.

entry.jurisdiction: Darlaston, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008 (FamilySearch collection 2285338, name-searchable) — Walsall civil registration district. Per loc_001, all Darlaston births are registered under the Walsall district, not West Bromwich. This is a co-equal search to pli_005, not a fallback: the boundary split means children born in Darlaston will appear in this district's index only. Both districts must be searched from the outset. The GRO index shows the mother's maiden name (Earnest) to confirm family identity.

entry.jurisdiction: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: England and Wales Death Registration Index, 1837–2007 (FamilySearch collection 2285341, name-searchable). Search for infant and child deaths with surname Grice in both the West Bromwich and Walsall registration districts from 1875 to 1900. A child who was born, registered, and died before the next census year would leave a birth index entry and a death index entry but no census trace. The death index entries, cross-referenced with the birth index, reveal the number and names of children who did not survive to any census. Required for completeness because the census alone cannot identify children who died between enumeration dates.

entry.jurisdiction: Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944 (FamilySearch collection 2364451, name-searchable) and England, Births and Christenings, 1538–1975 (collection 1473014, name-searchable). Baptism registers for West Bromwich and Darlaston Anglican parishes. Per loc_001, Darlaston All Saints chapelry was established in 1872 from the ancient St Lawrence parish; post-1872 baptisms may appear in either register. Search for Grice baptisms in West Bromwich and Darlaston 1875–1900. A baptism entry for an otherwise unknown child corroborates the civil registration birth and may supply additional detail.

entry.jurisdiction: Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: Staffordshire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1900 (Ancestry collection 62292, name-searchable) and England & Wales Non-Conformist Registers, 1567–1936 (Ancestry dbid=2972). Per loc_001, Darlaston had four Wesleyan Methodist places of worship; a child not found in Anglican registers may have been baptised in a Nonconformist chapel. The Nonconformist registers are held at The National Archives and indexed on Ancestry. This item is a fallback for pli_008 and also covers the Nonconformist gap that the FamilySearch Anglican search cannot address. Findmypast Staffordshire Baptisms, 1538–1900 is an additional alternative index.

entry.jurisdiction: Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
entry.rationale: British Newspaper Archive / Findmypast Staffordshire newspaper titles including the County Advertiser & Herald for Staffordshire and Worcestershire (1856–1907) and the Darlaston Weekly Times (1882–1887, Findmypast). Per loc_001, these papers may carry birth, death, and infant death notices for the Grice family. A birth announcement or mourning notice for an infant child may be the only surviving record of a child who died before civil registration was completed or before any census year. Particularly valuable for the 1882–1887 window when the Darlaston Weekly Times was in print.

- **Nonconformist registers**: Darlaston had four Wesleyan chapels; Ancestry holds the England & Wales Non-Conformist Registers, 1567–1936 (dbid=2972)
- **Newspapers**: Findmypast and British Newspaper Archive carry Staffordshire titles covering this period

1. Record types: census ✓, vital records (birth + death) ✓, church/baptism ✓, newspaper ✓ — broad enough

guardrail_shadow_violations.detail: person_evidence link written for new tree person(s) I1 with no prior same_person call: a brand-new identity should be scored before it is asserted (person-evidence/SKILL.md doctrine; issue #963). Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I1" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
